title: Red-Braised Turkey Lion's Head Meatballs with Bok Choy (红烧狮子头, hóngshāo shīzi tóu)
origin: Created in chat from pantry: bok choy, 1½ lb ground turkey, Chinese sauces and spices

steps.action: Stir the meatball mix hard in one direction until tacky, 2 to 3 min:
items: 3 scallions, whites minced (greens reserved for garnish)

sub: Beat in 1 Tbsp at a time

steps.action: Shape 8 balls with wet hands; brown in a Dutch oven over medium-high, 2 min per side, then set aside:

items: 1 large head bok choy, stems cut into 2 in pieces, leaves kept separate

steps.action: Fry the aromatics over medium, 30 sec:
Add the braising liquid, return the meatballs, and simmer covered on low, 20 min:
Add the bok choy stems and simmer covered, 5 min:
Add the leaves and cook until wilted and the meatballs reach 165 °F (74 °C), about 2 min:
Remove the meatballs and greens; thicken the sauce at a simmer, 1 min:
items: 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 Tbsp water

steps.action: Spoon the sauce over and garnish:

items: 1 Tbsp doubanjiang, fried with the aromatics, for a spicier Sichuan version

notes.text: Ive got a big head of bok choy and 1.5 lb of ground turkey. Come up with a Chinese inspired recipe. I have all the usual spices, plus these Chinese ones to pick from.

edits: Thai black soy (Dek Som Boon) is thick and sweet like molasses, so sugar is only 1 tsp; taste before adding more
Lean turkey dries out; the beaten-in water, egg, and cornstarch keep it tender. 93/7 is better than 99% lean
Fish sauce and turkey are departures from the traditional pork version
